reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.ξ -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: none directly; the random coefficients xi_i : Omega -> R of a simple predictable
process phi = sum_i xi_i 1_{(t_i,t_{i+1}]} (textbook). Faithful Lean: a family indexed by the
intervals (i < N), real-valued (scalar Brownian integral; vector/matrix integrands are handled
componentwise elsewhere), with, in the structure, the constraints that xi_i is
F_{t_i}-measurable (strongly measurable / measurable for the sigma-algebra F_{t_i} of the
filtration for which the integral is taken) and bounded or square-integrable. The field itself
is only the function; its meaning depends on those constraints being present in the structure.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.SimplePredictable.ξ (ItoSimpleIntegrand.lean:39-40)

Reading: a family indexed by the intervals (i < N), real-valued, constrained in the structure to
be F_{t_i}-measurable and bounded/L^2. Lean: xi : Fin N -> Omega -> R, one coefficient per
interval (consistent with eval and simpleIntegral); structure constraints xi_bounded and
xi_measurable (ambient). The F_{t_i}-measurability is NOT a constraint of the structure: it is a
hypothesis of the consumers (masterApprox_adapt for the master sequence; the L^2-membership and
adaptedness lemmas of simpleIntegral take it as an argument). As a projection, xi returns exactly
the coefficients xi_i. Representation choice: adaptedness is carried outside the structure,
harmless for the propositions because the only definition-level consumer imposes it.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Choices: (1) the coefficients carry only boundedness and ambient measurability; their
F_{t_i}-measurability is a hypothesis of the consumers (masterApprox_adapt supplies it for every
element of the master sequence, the only use in the propositions' definition closure), so every
coefficient that enters a stochastic integral of the propositions is adapted. (2) bounded rather
than square-integrable coefficients: bounded adapted simple processes are dense in the integrand
class, so the L^2 extension is unchanged.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement on substance. The reviewer records "faithful" for the projection and notes that
F_{t_i}-measurability is not required by the structure; I record "faithful with representation
choices" to put that point (adaptedness supplied by the consumers, masterApprox_adapt) and the
bounded-coefficient choice into the verdict detail. Labelling only.
